bridge/common_types/BurningTxData.title: BurningTxData
bridge/common_types/BurningTxData.description:
Parameters:
 - `destination_address_vk` is the `VerificationKeyHash` that the unlocked funds output will be for.
   This parameter is needed for verifying the proof.
 - `tx_id` is an unique identifier for the transaction that burned assets in the destination chain.
   For the validation, it must be equal to the one included in the `Redeemer` for the `txs_updater` spending script.
 - `transferred_amount` is the amount needed to construct the transferred value (which is of the opaque
   type `Value`). This parameter is needed for verifying the proof.
 - `transferred_asset_name` is the amount needed to construct the transferred value (which is of the
   opaque type `Value`). This parameter is needed for verifying the proof.
 - `transferred_asset_policy_id` is the amount needed to construct the transferred value (which is of
   the opaque type `Value`). This parameter is needed for verifying the proof.

bridge/common_types/TxsUpdaterDatum.title: TxsUpdaterDatum
bridge/common_types/TxsUpdaterDatum.description: This includes the merkle root corresponding to the NFT representing the transaction set that was processed by the updater validator

bridge/common_types/TxsUpdaterValidatorR.title: TxsUpdaterValidatorRedeemer
bridge/common_types/TxsUpdaterValidatorR.description:
Parameters:
 - `tx_id` is an unique identifier for a transaction.
 - `locked_assets_utxo_ref` is an `OutputReference` to the UTXO in the other chain which is being processed by the validator.
 - `tx_set_update_proof` is a Groth16 Proof that lets us update the validator's Merkle Tree accordingly.

cardano/address/Credential.title: Credential
cardano/address/Credential.description:
A general structure for representing an on-chain `Credential`.

 Credentials are always one of two kinds: a direct public/private key
 pair, or a script (native or Plutus).

cardano/address/PaymentCredential.title: PaymentCredential
cardano/address/PaymentCredential.description:
A general structure for representing an on-chain `Credential`.

 Credentials are always one of two kinds: a direct public/private key
 pair, or a script (native or Plutus).

minting/MintingValidatorRedeemer.title: MintingValidatorRedeemer
minting/MintingValidatorRedeemer.description:
The MintingValidatorRedeemer contains a Mithril certificate with a Cardano
 transactions snapshot plus a merkle proof of inclusion of the locking
 transaction in that snapshot. The certificate itself is validated against a
 phase-2 proof receipt present in the transaction inputs.

fields.title: network
fields.description: Cardano network

fields.title: protocol_version
fields.description:
Protocol Version (semver)
 Useful to achieve backward compatibility of the certificates (including of the multi signature)
 part of METADATA(p,n)

fields.title: protocol_parameters
fields.description:
Protocol parameters
 part of METADATA(p,n)

fields.title: initiated_at
fields.description:
Date and time when the certificate was initiated (in Mithril it was DateTime<Utc>)
 Represents the time at which the single signatures registration is opened
 part of METADATA(p,n)
 In Aiken we will only save the bytes after the Mithril operations, i.e. the result of:
 metadata.initiated_at.timestamp_nanos_opt().unwrap_or_default().to_be_bytes()

fields.title: sealed_at
fields.description:
Date and time when the certificate was sealed (in Mithril it was DateTime<Utc>)
 Represents the time at which the quorum of single signatures was reached so that they were aggregated into a multi signature
 part of METADATA(p,n)
 In Aiken we will only save the bytes after the Mithril operations, i.e. the result of:
 metadata.sealed_at.timestamp_nanos_opt().unwrap_or_default().to_be_bytes()

fields.title: signers
fields.description:
The list of the active signers with their stakes and verification keys
 part of METADATA(p,n)

fields.title: k
fields.description: Quorum parameter

fields.title: m
fields.description: Security parameter (number of lotteries)

fields.title: phi_f
fields.description:
f in phi(w) = 1 - (1 - f)^w, where w is the stake of a participant
 phi_f_fixed is a fixed decimal representation of phi_f (in Mithril)
 it is computed as `U8F24::from_num(self.phi_f)`. Therefore when we build a certificate
 in Aiken we must use the U8F24 representation, we can choose `ByteArray`

mithril/certificate_metadata/ProtocolVer.title: ProtocolVersion
mithril/certificate_metadata/ProtocolVer.description:
Mithril certificate metadata domain types and hashing helpers.

 This module owns the shape of the metadata carried inside a certificate and
 the exact hashing contract Mithril expects for protocol-parameter chaining.

fields.title: party_id
fields.description: Party identifier as in the stake distribution

fields.title: stake
fields.description: Amount of stake owned by the party

anyOf.title: MultiSignature
anyOf.description:
Every certificate which is not a genesis certificate has a `MultiSignature
 and includes a `SignedEntityType`.

anyOf.title: GenesisSignature
anyOf.description:
The `GenesisSignature` is the signature used for genesis certificate, which can be verified
 using Mithril's `GenesisVerificationKey`.

anyOf.title: GenesisDualSignature
anyOf.description:
Dual genesis signature carrying both the legacy Ed25519 half and the
 SNARK-friendly Schnorr half introduced by Mithril #3145.

mithril/certificate_signature/SignedEnti.title: SignedEntityType
mithril/certificate_signature/SignedEnti.description:
Mithril certificate-signature domain types.

 This module owns the signed-entity variants and their canonical
 serialization, which is shared anywhere certificate hashes must match the
 upstream Mithril implementation.
 Each `MithrilCertificate` must have a `SignedEntityType` in its signature. It is the entity
 that defines the purpose of the certificate.
 Only `MultiSignature` certificates have a `SignedEntityType`.

fields.title: hash
fields.description:
Hash of the current certificate
 Computed from the other fields of the certificate
 aka H(Cp,n))

fields.title: prev_hash
fields.description:
Hash of the previous certificate in the chain
 This is either the hash of the first certificate of the epoch in the chain
 Or the first certificate of the previous epoch in the chain (if the certificate is the first of its epoch)
 aka H(FC(n))
 It is not null only if the certificate is not a genesis certificate

fields.title: epoch
fields.description: Cardano chain epoch number

fields.title: metadata
fields.description:
Certificate metadata (this is necessary for doing the multisignature verification)
 aka METADATA(p,n)

fields.title: protocol_message
fields.description:
Structured message that is used to create the signed message
 aka MSG(p,n) U AVK(n-1)

fields.title: signed_message
fields.description:
Message that is signed by the signers.

 In this repo the legacy genesis and standard certificate fixtures still
 model this as lowercase ASCII hex bytes, matching the existing
 certificate-hash / Ed25519 path. The dual-genesis Jubjub helper decodes
 those bytes back to the raw 32-byte digest before binding them to the
 Groth16 public inputs `digest_hi` / `digest_low`.

 aka H(MSG(p,n) || AVK(n-1))

fields.title: aggregate_verification_key
fields.description:
Aggregate verification key
 The AVK used to sign during the current epoch
 aka AVK(n-2)

fields.title: aggregate_verification_key_snark
fields.description:
Aggregate verification key for the SNARK proof system.
 This is the AVK used to verify Lagrange-era aggregate signatures.

fields.title: signature
fields.description: Certificate signature

mithril/reduced_mithril_certificate/Redu.title: ReducedMithrilCertificate
mithril/reduced_mithril_certificate/Redu.description:
Reduced certificate state persisted on-chain for the bridge flows.

 The full Mithril certificate is too bulky to keep in datums, so the bridge
 stores only the fields needed for parent-state chaining and bridge mint
 validation.

phase1/Phase1Redeemer.title: Phase1Redeemer
phase1/Phase1Redeemer.description: Redeemer consumed by the phase-1 minting validator.

two_phase/two_phase_types/Phase1State.title: Phase1State
two_phase/two_phase_types/Phase1State.description:
Datum produced by TX1.

 - `rhs_prefix`:   compressed G1 partial accumulator (48 bytes)
 - `reduced_hash`: blake2b_256 of the serialised ReducedRedeemer (32 bytes)
 - `x1`:           transcript challenge x1 (32 bytes, little-endian scalar)
 - `x3`:           transcript challenge x3 (32 bytes, little-endian scalar)
 - `x4`:           transcript challenge x4 (32 bytes, little-endian scalar)
 - `v`:            precomputed blinding scalar (32 bytes, little-endian scalar)

two_phase/two_phase_types/Phase2Redeemer.title: Phase2Redeemer
two_phase/two_phase_types/Phase2Redeemer.description:
Phase-2 spend redeemer.

 - `Verify` completes the Halo2 verification and must mint the proof NFT.
 - `Recover` unlocks the UTxO for the signer of TX1 after the timeout.

two_phase/two_phase_types/Phase2State.title: Phase2State
two_phase/two_phase_types/Phase2State.description:
Datum consumed by the phase-2 spending validator.

 Wraps the proof-derived state with the recovery controls needed in TX2:
 - `phase1_signer`: signer allowed to reclaim the UTxO after timeout
 - `reclaim_after`: absolute POSIX time (ms) after which recovery is enabled
 - `statement_hash`: Mithril signed-message digest, carried directly as the
   second public input of the STM circuit and later certified by TX2

two_phase/two_phase_types/ProofReceiptDa.title: ProofReceiptDatum
two_phase/two_phase_types/ProofReceiptDa.description:
Datum carried by the phase-2 proof receipt output.

 This lets other contexts consume the NFT together with a statement hash
 that is bound to the Mithril signed message verified by the STM proof.

two_phase/two_phase_types/ReducedRedeeme.title: ReducedRedeemer
two_phase/two_phase_types/ReducedRedeeme.description:
Reduced redeemer consumed by TX2.

 Contains only the proof-derived G1 commitment points that are NOT
 verification-key constants, plus the PCS witness and f-commitment.

 Layout (flat tuple for minimal CBOR overhead):
   ( vanishing_g          -- compressed G1 (set 0 suffix, computed)
   , vanishing_rand       -- compressed G1 (set 0 suffix, from proof)
   , a1                   -- set 1
   , a2                   -- set 1
   , a3                   -- set 1
   , perm_d               -- set 1 (permutations_committed_d)
   , lookup_1             -- set 1
   , lookup_2             -- set 1
   , perm_a               -- set 2
   , perm_b               -- set 2
   , perm_c               -- set 2
   , perm_input_1         -- set 3
   , perm_input_2         -- set 3
   , f_commitment         -- PCS
   , pi_term              -- PCS witness
   )

zk/jubjub_schnorr_verification/JubjubSch.title: JubjubSchnorrProof
zk/jubjub_schnorr_verification/JubjubSch.description:
Prover-supplied data attesting a JubJub Schnorr signature via Groth16: the
 proof plus the public inputs of the dual-genesis circuit (the signer's
 verification key `u`/`v` and the signature's `response`/`challenge`, all as
 ASCII-decimal `ByteArray`s — see `jubjub_genesis_schnorr_proof_verifies`).
